items.statement: On duty days randomised to the structured checklist, the median time from alert to validation decision is at least 20 percent shorter than on usual-validation days, without more true events dismissed at the first alert.
items.rationale: Supported by one randomised comparison; the day-level design answers the director's question with existing logs.
items.risks: Contamination despite day randomisation; too few true events to judge safety formally.

items.statement: The checklist makes escalation decisions more consistent between epidemiologists.
items.rationale: Agencies with written procedures reported more consistent decisions.
items.risks: Consistency is hard to measure with six people.

items.statement: The checklist's sensitivity for true outbreaks exceeds 90 percent against panel review.
items.rationale: The accuracy framing the investigator considered.
items.risks: Panel review is a weak reference standard (claim c2).

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected, h3 kept to show why the accuracy framing was set aside.
